Optimal.Notes: A locked 40 fps at 40 Hz gives a smooth, tear-free experience that suits the game's pacing; medium settings preserve visual atmosphere without overloading the GPU. Ambient Occlusion is left off as it has a disproportionate cost in Unity-based games like this.

profiles.Summary: The Forest runs on Steam Deck via Proton with a gold/trending-platinum ProtonDB rating, suggesting most players get it working well with minimal tweaks. The Deck's RDNA 2 GPU comfortably exceeds the game's minimum and meets recommended specs, so stable 40–60 fps is achievable depending on settings and area complexity.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements (GTX 560 recommended, well within Deck GPU class) and the Unity engine's typical scaling behaviour on Deck. On first run, check frame rate in a dense forest clearing and inside caves — those are the heaviest scenarios — and drop to Optimal if the 60 fps cap proves unstable.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 at high settings is within reach in open areas, but expect dips toward 45 fps in dense forest or large mutant encounters; Shadow Distance and Quality are kept at Medium as they are the biggest GPU cost. Uncapped TDP lets the APU boost freely for best headroom.

Optimal.Notes: 40 Hz refresh with a 40 fps cap gives perfectly smooth, tear-free gameplay that feels noticeably better than 30 fps. Medium settings with FSR upscaling strike a good balance between visual quality and efficiency.

Occasional stutters reported on first-time shader compilation under Proton (pre-cache shaders via Steam settings to mitigate).
No native Linux build; runs via Proton — minor compatibility edge cases possible with mods or certain save states.

MaxPerformance.Notes: The Forest's modest GPU requirements mean the Deck can push native 1280x800 at high settings and still hit 60 fps in most areas; dense forest canopy may dip to the low 50s. Motion Blur is disabled as it adds no quality benefit on a handheld screen.
